**Diagnosis:** `parse_unquoted_value` (parser.py:123-125) strips comments with `re.sub(r"\s+#.*", "", part)`, which requires whitespace before `#`. But `_equal_sign` (`=[^\S\r\n]*`) already consumes the space after `=`, so for `KEY= # explanation` the remainder is `"# explanation"` — no preceding whitespace — so the comment isn't stripped and the value becomes `"# explanation"` instead of `""`.

**Change plan:** In `parse_unquoted_value`, change the strip regex to also match a `#` at the start of the remainder, e.g. `re.sub(r"(?:^|\s+)#.*", "", part).rstrip()`. This makes `KEY= # explanation` → `""`, while `KEY=#literal` and `KEY=a#b` stay literal (no preceding whitespace), and quoting/exports/ordinary comments are untouched. Add parser tests covering these three cases.
